items.context: @coinbureau (Coin Bureau, 1.134.619 seguidores): "Lyn Alden just said 'Bitcoin is dead' exactly 4 years to the day after she said it in 2022. Bitcoin hit its bear market bottom that same day, near $15,600... Within 3 years, it hit a record $126,000, an 8x. Now, after a 56% fall from that record, she's said it again." Post de ~2,7 h con 299 likes, 61 respuestas, 22 reposts y 33.482 vistas. Ángulo: señales de piso y temperatura de mercado.
items.suggested_text:
The interesting part isn't the quote, it's what the market looked like each time someone could say it with a straight face. Late 2022 was a textbook cold reading: price under the 200-week average, MVRV around or below 1, most recent buyers underwater and a deep drawdown from the high.

Sentiment tends to bottom alongside those metrics, not after them. That's why I track a Market Temperature index that blends MVRV, price vs the 200-week average, distance from the ATH and volatility-adjusted 90-day momentum, 25% each. Over the last 364 days it went from 99.29 to 0.67.

A cold reading has never been a timing signal on its own. But it's worth noticing how rarely "dead" gets said when the gauges are running hot.
